attempts.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: blocker_moved is wrong. It scans cells left of every door instead of the fixed cell in front of the door on the start side, and its nested conditionals/`else` expression make the semantics unreliable; per the grounding, the ball starts at (dx - 1, dy) for the single door at (dx, dy), so it must return false only when a ball sits on that specific cell (a carried ball counts as moved, since it is not on the grid). Rewrite it as a simple scan: find the unique door at (dx, dy) via a guarded grid scan, then return not any guarded cell at (dx - 1, dy) is a ball, following the documented truth condition `not any(c is not None and c.type == 'ball' for c in [env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy)])`. has_door_key is correct and needs no change.

NO CHANGES NEEDED. Both declared propositions are covered exactly once with matching names, each predicate takes only `env` and is expression-only. `blocker_moved` locates the unique door and checks the cell at (dx-1, dy) for a ball, matching the documented layout where the ball starts directly left of the door; a carried ball is off-grid so it correctly counts as moved, and it is a pure current-observation condition that correctly turns false again if the ball is dropped back. `has_door_key` guards `env.carrying` before reading attributes and matches the carried key's color against the door found by a guarded full-grid scan, matching the documented truth conditions. Only allowed builtins and documented API attributes are used; no mutation, no previous-valuation use (neither proposition is an event), and no invented API.

NO CHANGES NEEDED. Every declared proposition has exactly one predicate with an expression-only body guarded correctly, persistent propositions read only the current observation, and key_lost correctly compares against the previous valuation, stays false on the first step, and requires the door closed, matching the documented semantics.
